description:
Found during the fz-21x.25 cold review; reproduced at main-side baseline 4f49465f9 and at main cb9f7d440, so it predates that change and does not run through entry dispatch (the backend dump shows use/1 has no entry_dispatch).

    defp mk(n), do: {fn x -> x + n end, n}
    defp use({f, k}), do: f.(k)
    def main() do
      before = Process.heap_alloc_stats()
      a = use(mk(5))
      later = Process.heap_alloc_stats()
      dbg(a)
      dbg({before[:struct_allocs], later[:struct_allocs]})
    end

interp: 10 / {0, 0}. run and build: a large garbage integer such as 936748763916397248 / {0, 0}. It reproduces with the tuple forced onto the heap as well (a second clause of a different arity makes mk/1 return a union, one struct alloc, still garbage), so the defect is in how the closure lane of a tuple field is delivered to the call, not in lane-form transport. The closure captures n and is applied to k; the capture or the argument arrives wrong natively.

Where to look: direct-callable capture transport of a tuple FIELD (transport_field_views hands back Transport{Callable} for a callable field; direct_closure_capture_lanes / lower call of a callable bound from a tuple field), and the boxed-closure path (p3e variant). Signal: the program above as a behavior fixture on all three doors, expected 10 and 0 struct allocs; today red on run and build.
title: [BUG] A closure carried in a tuple field is called with a garbage argument on run and build; interp answers correctly
